agent: Claude Code (CLAUDE.md, this repository) — wire a GATE agent decider's completion path (was dead code)
summary_for_principal: Continuing the live evaluation: the previous fix closed one permission gap; checking the sibling case (an AI agent voting on an approval gate, not just running a step) found a bigger one. The code to validate an agent's approval vote — checking its evidence is real and that it isn't approving its own work — was fully written months ago but never actually connected to anything. There was no way for an agent's vote to ever reach the engine at all. Built the missing connection: an agent's vote now goes through the same permission check as everything else, then through that existing validation, before it counts. Also had to fix a second, smaller bug this uncovered along the way: the "can't approve your own work" check was comparing the wrong things and would never have caught anything even once wired up. Proved it now does, with a test where the same identity produces a recommendation and then tries to approve it — correctly blocked. Seven new tests total, one exercising the full realistic path (produce, then a different identity approves, run completes). Full suite: 299 tests pass.

also.reason: check_agent_decision and resolve_gate already existed, correctly written, from WP-02 step 4 — confirmed by reading directly that they were never called from run.py before this fix (grep for check_agent_decision across the module found zero call sites).
Three new end-to-end tests (happy path, no-permission fallback, separation-of-duty) proving the wiring works, plus reused the two STEP-side permission tests from the immediately prior run.
The immediately prior run record's own flags[] entry (gate-decider-tool-dispatch-unchecked) named exactly this as unverified; this run confirms it was real and closes it.

interpretation.ask_as_given: Keep fixing as I find them (your selection from the scope-decision question).
interpretation.read_as: Continue the live evaluation and close verified gaps as they surface, including ones larger than the first (the permission-only fix). You were shown the shape of the problem (agent gate decisions have no completion path at all, and the separation-of-duty code for them is dead) before choosing this option, so proceeding to design and build the completion path is exactly what was asked for, not an expansion of it.

filled_in.gap: Neither the spec nor gates.py's own code says HOW an agent decider's completion should reach the engine (which of next()/report()/decide() carries it, what shape the payload takes) or what should happen when a decider Tool's permission is refused mid-multi-decider-sequence (unlike a STEP, which has no fallback decider to try instead).
filled_in.assumed: Routed it through report() (gates.py's own docstring already says agent deciders need a round trip through report(), grouping them with STEP's Tool hand-off) rather than inventing a fourth engine call. For permission refusal, chose INDETERMINATE (this decider simply doesn't count, exactly resolve_gate's own existing behaviour for an agent decision that fails validation) over ending the whole run FORBIDDEN (the STEP precedent) — explained fully in decisions[] below.
filled_in.grounded_in: gates.py's own docstring ("both need a round trip through next()/report()/decide()"); resolve_gate's own pre-existing logic, which already treats an INDETERMINATE decider outcome as "ask the next one, or pause if none left" — extending that existing fallback rather than adding a second, different failure mode.
filled_in.reversal_cost: Cheap — additive (a new dispatch branch in report(), a new parameter thread through _drive/_advance_gate); no existing behaviour changed for STRICT processes or gates with no agent decider, confirmed by the full pre-existing suite passing unchanged.

filled_in.gap: check_agent_decision needs `produced_by: Mapping[str, str]` (which identity produced each reviewed state path) and `agent_session_id`, but nothing in the engine built `produced_by`, and no existing convention identified "which identity performed an AGENT-performed step" durably (the spec's own quoted `performed_by` example, `AGENT:interrogate@1`, carries no identity at all).
filled_in.assumed: Extended `performed_by`'s format for AGENT-performed STEP outcomes to `AGENT:<tool-ref>::<identity>` (double colon, not the spec-quoted single form) — chosen because this codebase's own identity strings already contain single colons (`user:iain`), and a CODE Tool's own `module:function` ref does too, making a single-colon separator genuinely ambiguous to parse back apart; `::` does not appear in either. `_producer_identity()` parses it back out to build `produced_by` from `_drive`'s replay, which already re-derives everything else from durable records the same way.
filled_in.grounded_in: spec S12.2 ("performed_by ... an opaque identity string") — opaque to the PORT's own contract, not to this module's own internal convention for constructing it, which record.py's docstring does not forbid extending.
filled_in.reversal_cost: Cheap — localized to three call sites constructing the string and one helper parsing it back; a future AttemptRecord schema change adding a dedicated identity field would let this be removed without changing check_agent_decision's own contract.

decisions.headline: A GATE agent decider's completion is routed through report(), which forwards the raw decision into _drive() as `pending_decision` rather than validating it directly.
decisions.problem: Validating an agent's decision (S7.6: evidence resolves to a real value in the run, no deciding on your own work) needs the run's current state and `produced_by` history — which report() itself has no way to reconstruct (S12.1: nothing held between calls; only _drive's own replay rebuilds it). STEP's report() avoided this because check_controls needs only the tool and its output, not run state.
options_rejected: Have report() itself replay the whole run to rebuild state before validating: rejected — duplicates _drive's own replay loop a second time, the exact kind of copy CLAUDE.md's "hold conventions once" warns against, and risks the two copies drifting apart on the next change to either.

Add a fourth top-level engine call (e.g. `decide_agent()`) instead of extending report(): rejected — gates.py's own docstring already describes agent deciders as using report(), and inventing a fourth call not named anywhere in S12.1 is exactly the kind of code-level invention CLAUDE.md says to avoid when the spec doesn't already describe it; skip() (the one precedent for a 4th call in this codebase) was different — S6 describes skip's own behaviour fully, just not by that call name, whereas nothing describes a fourth call for this.
decisions.cost_to_change: The pending_decision parameter is additive and defaults to None; every existing next()/report()/decide() caller is unaffected.

evidence.claim: Before this fix, `check_agent_decision` (gates.py) had zero call sites anywhere in the engine — confirmed by grep across src/sulis_workflows/ before writing any code.
evidence.source: grep -rn "check_agent_decision" src/sulis_workflows/, run before this fix.

evidence.claim: The wiring works end to end: a produced value, reviewed by a DIFFERENT identity with grounded evidence, resolves PERMIT and the run reaches COMPLETE.

decisions.revisit_if: A future work package needs an agent decider's decision to arrive from somewhere other than a caller that already knows how to call report() (e.g. a purely async/webhook-driven host) — not requested now.

decisions.headline: A GATE agent decider whose Tool has no permission, or is refused, becomes INDETERMINATE for that decider rather than ending the whole run FORBIDDEN.
decisions.problem: The STEP-side fix (immediately prior run) ends the whole run FORBIDDEN when a Tool's permission is absent or refused, because a STEP has exactly one Tool and no fallback. A GATE, by its own design, has multiple deciders in a declared order — treating an unauthorized decider as a hard stop would let one misconfigured or under-permissioned decider block a gate that could still resolve via policy or a person, which no part of S7.6 asks for.
options_rejected: Mirror the STEP precedent exactly (end FORBIDDEN): rejected — defeats the gate's own multi-decider fallback design for no reason the spec gives; a gate reviewer that lacks permission is a configuration problem to flag, not a reason to end the entire run for every other decider and every other reviewer too.

Silently skip this decider (act as if it were never declared, moving straight to the next without recording anything): rejected — violates S12.2 ("every attempt of every node is one write-once record") and leaves no audit trail of why this decider's vote is missing.
decisions.cost_to_change: Localized to the one `if permission_rationale is not None:` branch in _advance_gate's NEEDS_AGENT handling.

evidence.claim: resolve_gate already treats an INDETERMINATE outcome as "this decider didn't decide, ask the next one (or pause if none left)" — confirmed by reading resolve_gate directly; using the same verdict for a permission-refused decider reuses this existing fallback rather than adding a second, different kind of failure the rest of the gate machinery doesn't already know how to handle.

A gate whose only decider has no permission correctly falls through to AWAITING_DECISION (paused, asking for a person) rather than silently permitting or crashing, and the INDETERMINATE record carries a rationale naming the permission gap.

decisions.revisit_if: A future spec revision describes an explicit failure mode for an unauthorized gate decider (e.g. a dedicated FORBIDDEN-at-gate ending) — not currently written.

decisions.headline: `performed_by` for an AGENT-performed STEP now carries the identity as `AGENT:<ref>::<identity>` (double colon), used only internally by `_producer_identity()` to rebuild `produced_by`.
decisions.problem: See interpretation[].filled_in[1] above — no existing signal identified which identity performed a STEP, and a naive single-colon suffix is ambiguous against this codebase's own identity/ref conventions.
options_rejected: Add a dedicated `identity` field to AttemptRecord/RecordsPort instead of encoding it in `performed_by`: rejected for this pass — a port-contract change ripples into every adapter and every existing caller of record_attempt/get_attempts, and is a bigger, riskier change than this fix's actual target (wiring the dead-code validation path) needed; flagged below as a cleaner alternative for a future pass.

Leave `performed_by` unchanged and reconstruct identity some other way (e.g. a side-channel cache): rejected — nothing else durable exists to reconstruct it from on a pure replay (S12.1's own "nothing held between calls"), so it has to live in the one durable field that already exists.
decisions.cost_to_change: If AttemptRecord ever gains a dedicated identity field, `_producer_identity()` and the three call sites constructing the `::`-suffixed string can be deleted together without touching check_agent_decision's own contract, which only ever receives the already-extracted bare identity.

evidence.claim: A single-colon separator is provably ambiguous: this session's own EngineContext.identity values throughout testing are `"user:iain"`-shaped (containing a colon), and CODE Tool refs are `module:function`-shaped (also containing a colon) — the first version of this fix used a single colon and the separation-of-duty test failed silently (compared full strings, never matched) until this was caught and fixed.
evidence.source: This session's own draft-then-fix cycle: test_gate_agent_decider_cannot_decide_on_its_own_work failed on first write (produced_by stored the whole `AGENT:produce@1.0.0:agent:same-session` string, compared against the bare identity `agent:same-session`, never equal), diagnosed, and fixed by switching to `::`.

decisions.revisit_if: A future work package touches RecordsPort's own schema for another reason — a dedicated identity field would be the more honest long-term shape; worth doing then rather than as a standalone migration now.

untouched.divergence: If report() is called for a gate that, by the time _drive reaches it, is no longer awaiting that specific agent decider (a stale hand-off, a duplicate call, wrong node), the decision is silently dropped rather than raising — the caller gets the gate's actual current answer instead, which is safe (nothing is corrupted or wrongly applied) but not loud.
untouched.why_not_now: Detecting this properly needs the same full run-state reconstruction _report_gate_decision was specifically designed to avoid duplicating (see decisions[] above); flagged as a known, minor rough edge rather than fixed, since nothing observed in this evaluation exercises the misuse case.

lessons.maxim: A validation function that exists, is correctly written, and has its own unit tests can still be completely inert if nothing in the actual call graph reaches it — grep for real call sites, not just for the function's own test file, before trusting that a described check is actually enforced.
lessons.incident: check_agent_decision (gates.py) was written in WP-02 step 4, is correctly implemented, and test_gates.py tests it directly and thoroughly — every signal an engineer would normally trust that this check is live. It had zero callers anywhere in the actual engine. Found only by trying to complete a real gate decision end to end, not by reading gates.py or its tests in isolation.
lessons.destination: Before claiming any validation/check/control is enforced in this engine, grep for its actual call sites in engine/run.py (the only place that drives real execution), not just for its own unit tests.
lessons.proposed_check: tests/engine/test_run.py::test_gate_agent_decider_permit_with_evidence_completes_via_report and its two sibling tests, which are the first tests in this repository that exercise check_agent_decision through the real engine rather than by calling it directly.

lessons.maxim: When encoding structured information into a string field for internal bookkeeping, check whether the substrings you plan to split on can already appear inside the values themselves — in a codebase whose own identity convention already uses the delimiter you reach for first, that delimiter is not safe.
lessons.incident: The first draft used a single `:` to append identity to `performed_by`. This codebase's own EngineContext.identity values are already colon-shaped (`"user:iain"`), so the resulting string had four colon-separated segments with no way to know where the Tool ref ended and the identity began — caught only because the separation-of-duty test was written to actually assert the check fires, not just that report() returns without error.
lessons.destination: Any future encoding of structured data into one of this codebase's opaque string fields (performed_by, decided_by, permission strings): check the existing value conventions for the delimiter first.
lessons.proposed_check: _producer_identity()'s own docstring in engine/run.py, which states the reasoning inline at the point future readers would need it.

ready_now: A GATE's `agent` decider now has a real completion path: permission-checked, evidence-checked, and separation-of-duty-checked, matching what gates.py's own code was written to do from WP-02 step 4 but was never connected to run() until this fix.

parked.item: report() called for a gate no longer awaiting the decision it's given silently drops it instead of raising.
parked.trigger: A real caller hits this in practice (a duplicate report() call, a race between two reviewers) and needs to know their decision was dropped rather than just re-reading the gate's current state.
parked.detail: Safe today — nothing is corrupted, the caller just gets the gate's true current answer back. Only becomes a real problem if a host builds a UI that assumes a report() call always either succeeds or raises.
